item.title: The Downward Arc of Donald Trump, With Ruth Ben-Ghiat
item.description: An expert on authoritarianism explains the ways strongmen consolidate power - and how they lose it

item.title: Closing Al-Aqsa Mosque during Ramadan sets a dangerous precedent
item.description: Muslims fear that Israel, which said the closure was over security, will misuse the situation to further tighten the Israeli police grip on the mosque and its management.

item.title: Deportations surge, aid collapses and faith groups in Latin America struggle to respond
item.description: 'There simply isn’t enough capacity even for the local community. It’s much harder with a population that has been abandoned in places that are extremely difficult,' said Karen Perez, the country director for Jesuit Refugee Service in Mexico.

item.title: Explosives thrown near New York City mayor’s residence investigated as ‘ISIS-related terrorism’
item.description: The devices were hurled during raucous counterprotests Saturday near Gracie Mansion during a “Stop the Islamic Takeover of New York City” event led by the far right activist Jake Lang.

item.title: Muslim leaders call closure of Al-Aqsa Mosque during Ramadan politically motivated
item.description: Worshippers' access to Israel’s holy sites came to a sudden halt last week amid safety concerns as Iran retaliated to the joint US-Israeli attack.

item.title: Where things stand after another weekend of war
item.description: The Islamic Republic's war strategy now has a new commander, and the powerful paramilitary Revolutionary Guard has pledged allegiance.

item.title: Today’s obsession with authenticity isn’t new – being true to yourself has troubled philosophers for centuries
item.description: Contemporary culture seems obsessed with authenticity – but the question of how to be ‘sincere’ in modern society has troubled philosophers for centuries.

item.title: Whom Does Your God Love? A Jewish Case for the Stranger. With Shai Held.
item.description: Who is the stranger in the Bible? Some Americans would be surprised.

item.title: How one Chinese American healed from growing up in Western evangelicalism
item.description: The book, releasing April 7, uses the Japanese art of Kintsugi — repairing broken pottery with gold — as a metaphor for a faith that acknowledges wounds rather than hiding them.

item.title: The goal of National Women’s History Month should be to make misogyny history
item.description: Imagine what women could accomplish if they did not have to contend with misogyny every day.
